sections.title: Market Pulse: Record-Setting Week Closes on a High Note

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Extend Gains, Capping a Robust Week of Trading
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indices ended Friday's session with gains, successfully closing out a record-setting week. The S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, and Nasdaq Composite all posted advances, driven by a rebound in technology stocks and easing concerns over OpenAI's revenue projections. Despite persistent inflation worries and geopolitical tensions, investor sentiment remained positive, pushing equities near all-time highs.

items.headline: Moderna Rallies on Nasdaq 100 Inclusion and Biotech Demand
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) saw a significant jump, climbing 14.2%, following its addition to the Nasdaq 100 index. The biotech sector generally gained amidst fears of a global pneumonic plague spread.

items.headline: Crown Castle Surges on SpaceX Spectrum Deal Optimism
items.summary: Crown Castle ($CCI) gained 15.6% after SpaceX announced a deal to acquire wireless spectrum from Grain Management, which signals increased demand for wireless infrastructure.

items.headline: Humana Jumps on Improved Medicare Advantage Rating
items.summary: Humana ($HUM) surged 13% after the insurer reported encouraging data regarding its Medicare Advantage quality ratings and received an analyst upgrade.

items.headline: T-Mobile US Drops on SpaceX Competition Concerns
items.summary: T-Mobile US ($TMUS) fell 13.27% to $148.58, as news of SpaceX's spectrum acquisition sparked competitive concerns for traditional wireless carriers.

items.headline: AT&T Slides as SpaceX Spectrum Deal Threatens Competition
items.summary: AT&T ($T) closed down 9.81% at $22.17, reacting negatively to the SpaceX spectrum deal which raised fears of increased competition in the wireless market.

items.headline: Verizon Communications Impacted by New Wireless Competition
items.summary: Verizon Communications ($VZ) dropped 8.75% to $41.65, with investors reacting to potential competitive threats from SpaceX's entry into the wireless spectrum landscape.

items.headline: Apple Slips Amid Reports of Reduced iPhone Component Orders
items.summary: Apple ($AAPL) declined 1.11% to $336.64 after reports indicated the company reduced component orders for its upcoming iPhone series, citing weak demand.

items.headline: Real Estate Leads Gains, Communication Services Lags
items.summary: Real estate emerged as the top-performing sector, advancing 1.88% on Friday. Conversely, Communication Services was the worst-performing sector, declining 0.4%, heavily impacted by news in the wireless industry. Energy stocks also saw significant gains, with the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) rising 3%. Software and cybersecurity stocks attracted strong buying interest, while the semiconductor sector showed mixed performance.

items.headline: Consumer Sentiment Continues Decline in October
items.summary: The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index for October fell to a preliminary reading of 46.3 from 48.1 in September, missing forecasts. This marks the fifth consecutive monthly decline, attributed to sustained high gas prices and rising borrowing costs impacting consumers.

items.headline: Jobless Claims Show Slight Decrease
items.summary: The Labor Department reported that jobless claims totaled 197,000 for the week ending October 3, a decrease of 2,000 from the previous week's revised level of 199,000. The four-week moving average also saw a decrease, signaling a slight improvement in the labor market.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Rise, Oil Prices Tick Higher
items.summary: The yield on the 10-year Treasury note climbed to 5.24% on Friday, following swings throughout the day. Brent crude oil ticked higher, settling at $104.72 per barrel, up 0.4%, with prices stabilizing after President Trump indicated productive discussions with Iran, easing earlier geopolitical tensions.

items.headline: Q3 Earnings Season Kicks Off Next Week with Major Banks
items.summary: Third-quarter earnings season is set to gain momentum next week, with major U.S. banks including JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and Citigroup scheduled to report results. Analysts anticipate robust corporate profits, with S&P 500 earnings expected to jump by over 30% for the quarter. Semiconductor, energy, and technology sectors are projected to show particularly strong earnings growth.

items.headline: Fed Minutes Reveal Continued Focus on 2% Inflation Target
items.summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's September FOMC meeting, released this week, indicated that policymakers remain committed to bringing inflation down to the 2% target. A majority of officials anticipate at least one more interest rate hike before the year-end.
